  **Action**: #5056 [BUG api MEDIUM] The REST BGP routes endpoint (`/api/routing/bgp?type=routes`, `bgpHandler` in pkg/api/routing.go) materialized the ENTIRE upstream RIB before responding. It called `frr.GetBGPRoutes`, which ran `vtysh "show bgp ipv4 unicast"` and buffered ALL of vtysh stdout into one growable string (`realExecutor.Vtysh`, pkg/frr/vtysh.go) plus a parsed `[]BGPRoute` — hundreds of MB for a full internet table (~1M routes) on a RAM-constrained firewall, BEFORE the first byte went out. The #4708/#5232 work streamed only the DOWNSTREAM writer + added a per-1024-chunk client-cancel check, but the already-completed vtysh work upstream was unbounded and uncancellable. Fix (bound the materialization end-to-end): added `VtyshStream(ctx, command) (io.ReadCloser, func() error, error)` to the `frrExecutor` interface — `realExecutor` runs `exec.CommandContext` with a `StdoutPipe` so stdout is streamed, not buffered, and ctx-cancel kills vtysh. New `Manager.StreamBGPRoutes(ctx, limit, fn)` (pkg/frr/status_parse.go) scans that pipe with a bounded `bufio.Scanner`, parses each line via the shared `parseBGPRouteLine` helper (extracted from GetBGPRoutes so both interpret the table identically), delivers each route to `fn`, stops after `limit` routes (reporting `truncated`), and cancels vtysh on ctx-cancellation or an `fn` error. `bgpHandler` now streams via StreamBGPRoutes with a `maxBGPRoutes`=100000 cap: peak memory is O(1) in table size, a client disconnect / downstream write failure (now checked — the `bw.Flush()` return is no longer discarded) aborts the scan AND cancels vtysh, and when the cap trips a trailing `... table truncated at N routes; use the CLI 'show route protocol bgp' for the full table` notice is appended inside the JSON `output` string (envelope shape unchanged; only present when truncated, so the non-truncated wire format is byte-identical to #4708). The handler emits the 200 + envelope prefix LAZILY on the first route so an upstream vtysh START failure still surfaces as a clean 500. GetBGPRoutes is unchanged (still used by the CLI/gRPC show paths that render the whole result). Fail-on-revert test `TestBGPRoutesEndpointCapTruncates` (pkg/api/bgp_routes_cap_5056_test.go) drives the endpoint via the fake-executor seam with a 50-route table and a lowered cap (10), asserting exactly 10 route lines + the truncation notice + the over-cap route ABSENT + a well-formed envelope. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: disabling the `count >= limit` cap in StreamBGPRoutes made the endpoint stream all 50 routes → "rendered 50 route lines, want exactly the cap 10" + "truncation notice missing" + "over-cap route present" all FAIL; restored to green. The existing `bgp_routes_stream_4708_test.go` (wire-format + non-buffering) and `api_ctx_cancel_5232_5233_test.go` (client-cancel abort) now exercise the streaming path too (the api/frr/daemon test fakes gained a `VtyshStream` method) and stay green. Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; `go test ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/frr/... ./pkg/daemon/...` all ok; gofmt clean. Docs: pkg/api/README.md bgpHandler bullet + pkg/frr/README.md (vtysh.go/status_parse.go file-table entries and the "no streaming" note) updated to describe the upstream-streaming + cap/truncation contract. - **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
  **Action**: #5389 [BUG ddns/route53 MEDIUM] `route53Backend.UpsertLease` issued a bare full-RRset UPSERT — Route 53 `UPSERT` create-or-replaces the ENTIRE resource-record set at name+type, so a single-value change batch silently DELETED any co-resident FOREIGN A/AAAA (a manually-managed round-robin member, or another host's A at the same FQDN). This was the Route 53 arm of #3739 (Cloudflare + RFC 2136 were fixed; Route 53 was deferred as M07 and never implemented). Fix (ownership-scoped read-modify-write, mirroring the Cloudflare/RFC 2136 value-specific replace): both publish and withdraw now first `ListResourceRecordSets`-read the live RRset (new `listRRSet` + `listRRSetsXML`; a SigV4-signed GET with an EXACT name+type match so a Route 53 lexically-next neighbour set reads back as found=false) and change ONLY xpf's own value. `UpsertLease`: `mergeUpsertValues` keeps every current member except xpf's own prior value (`rec.PrevAddr`), adds `rec.Addr`, and UPSERTs the merged set — a live set already equal to the desired one (values + TTL) is a no-op; a first publish onto a foreign name is additive; a renumber with a lost prior value leaks a stale xpf row rather than clobbering a foreign one. `DeleteLease`: strip `rec.Addr` from the live set — absent set / xpf-value-absent ⇒ idempotent no-op (no change issued); foreign members remain ⇒ UPSERT the reduced set at the LIVE TTL; xpf's value sole member ⇒ DELETE the whole RRset (exact live-TTL match). The #2771 already-gone-DELETE idempotency (`r53DeleteAlreadyGone`) is preserved for the residual race where the record disappears between the List and the whole-RRset DELETE. `buildChangeBatch`/`change` generalized to take an explicit value list + TTL. CONCURRENCY CAVEAT documented in code + PR: Route 53 has no compare-and-swap for `ChangeResourceRecordSets`, so the RMW is not atomic — a foreign member written between the List and the change is not observed; the Surface A per-RG HA gate makes xpf a single writer for the name (same residual window the Cloudflare/RFC 2136 fixes accept). Fail-on-revert tests (backend_route53_test.go, rewritten onto a stateful `r53FakeAPI` that models GET-list + POST-change RRset semantics): `TestRoute53UpsertPreservesForeignRecord`, `TestRoute53RenumberPreservesForeign`, `TestRoute53DeletePreservesForeign` seed a co-resident foreign value and assert it SURVIVES publish/renumber/withdraw while xpf's value is set/renumbered/removed. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: reverting `UpsertLease` to the bare single-value UPSERT and `DeleteLease` to the bare single-value DELETE made all three FAIL ("UPSERT must carry the merged RRset ... got 1 values", "FOREIGN A was clobbered on renumber", "must not DELETE a shared RRset, got deletes=1"); restored to green. Added idempotent-no-op, ownership-conflict-no-op, absent-idempotent, raced-gone-idempotent, genuine-error-retry, and exact-match-list-filter coverage. Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; `go test ./pkg/ddns/...` ok (14 Route53 tests + full package); `go vet ./pkg/ddns/...` clean; gofmt clean. Docs: pkg/ddns/README.md file-table entry, the Cloudflare cross-reference, the #3739 per-provider co-resident section (Route 53 moved DEFERRED→implemented), and the #2771 already-gone note updated to describe the RMW + concurrency caveat. No cluster smoke (external DDNS control-plane path, no forwarding effect).

Two-layer fix (the prior attempt #5388 did only layer 1 and REGRESSED the callers). LAYER 1 (backend, additive on #5387's StreamBGPRoutes which is untouched): `routeReader.GetRoutes`/`GetRoutesForTable`/`GetAllTableRoutes` (pkg/routing/routes.go) now `errors.Join` each per-family netlink failure into the returned error, tagged with the family (`inet`/`inet6` via new `familyName` helper) plus table id / routing-instance name, and STILL return the successful family's entries; `GetAllTableRoutes` joins the main-table + per-instance errors (previously `continue`d and dropped the whole instance table) while still appending every table it could read; `frr.GetRouteDetailJSON` (pkg/frr/status_parse.go) joins per-command vtysh + JSON-parse failures tagged with the failing `show ip/ipv6 route json` command. Contract: non-nil error + non-empty slice = PARTIAL. LAYER 2 (callers — the half #5388 got wrong): every `show route` render caller now renders the partial AND emits a non-fatal `warning: partial route display (some address families unavailable): <err>` line instead of `return`ing the error and dropping the ENTIRE display (which, once the backend returns non-nil on partial, would break all of `show route` on a transient single-family hiccup — strictly worse than the old swallow).   **Action**: #5066 [BUG cli MEDIUM] `clear security flow session summary` (or `brief`, or `sort-by bytes`) parsed clean and cleared EVERY session on both HA nodes (fail-open destructive parse). The shared show/clear filter parser (`parseSessionFilter`, pkg/cli/session_filter.go) recognized the presentation tokens `summary`/`brief`/`sort-by` and set their display flags WITHOUT a parseErr, but `hasFilter()` deliberately excludes those three (they are display modifiers, not selectors), so on the clear path (`cli_clear.go` handleClearSecurity flow/session) `hasFilter()` returned false → `ClearAllSessions()` PLUS an unfiltered `clearPeerSessions(nil)` — the most destructive path — fired for a pasted show-syntax token. The remote `cli` clear parser (cmd/cli/clear.go) already rejected these via its `default` case; only the local interactive CLI was fail-open. Fix (selector-only clear parser, fail-closed): split `parseSessionFilter` into a shared `parseSessionFilterMode(args, clearMode bool)` with two entry points — `parseSessionFilter` (show, clearMode=false) and new `parseClearSessionFilter` (clear, clearMode=true). In clearMode the `summary`/`brief`/`sort-by` cases call `setParseErr(errDisplayModifierOnClear(tok))` instead of setting the display flag; `hasFilter()` already returns true when `parseErr != nil`, so a rejected token routes into `clearFilteredSessions` → `validate()` returns the error BEFORE any Iterate/Delete/ClearAll runs — neither clear method is invoked. `cli_clear.go` now calls `parseClearSessionFilter(args[2:])`. An EXACTLY-empty token list remains the only clear-all selector. Also hardened the SHOW path: `sort-by <value>` now validates the key is `bytes`|`packets` (an unknown value previously degraded silently to a plain per-session list instead of the requested top-talkers view) via a new parseErr surfaced through the existing showFlowSession `validate()`. Fail-on-revert tests (pkg/cli/cli_clear_flow_display_reject_test.go): a `clearCountDP` cliRuntime counts `ClearAllSessions`/`IterateSessions` calls; `TestClearFlowSessionRejectsDisplayModifiers` drives `clear security flow session {summary|brief|sort-by bytes|sort-by packets|protocol tcp summary}` and asserts each returns an error with BOTH counters at 0; `TestClearFlowSessionEmptyStillClearsAll` proves the no-arg path still calls ClearAllSessions exactly once; `TestParseClearSessionFilterRejectsDisplayTokens` asserts the clear parser sets parseErr/hasFilter/validate-error for the three tokens, the show parser still accepts them, and the show parser now rejects `sort-by garbage`. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: reverting the clear call site to `parseSessionFilter` made all five reject-subtests FAIL with output "0 IPv4 and 0 IPv6 session entries cleared" (and "matching sessions cleared" for the filter+summary case) — i.e. the destructive clear-all fired; restored → PASS. Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; `go test ./pkg/cli/... ./cmd/cli/...` all ok; gofmt clean. Docs: docs/junos-cli-reference.md "Security: Flow Sessions" gained a bullet documenting the clear-takes-selectors-only fail-closed invariant. No cluster smoke (control-plane CLI parse path; the fix PREVENTS a destructive dataplane action rather than changing forwarding).

  **Action**: #5121 [BUG lldp MEDIUM] The LLDP `Manager` lifecycle transitions `Apply` (config commit) and `Stop` (daemon shutdown) had NO lifecycle mutex. `Apply` wrote `m.cancel` and called `m.wg.Add(1)` per interface with no lifecycle lock; `Stop` read `m.cancel`, snapshotted `m.sessions`, and called `m.wg.Wait()`. Only `m.mu` guarded the neighbor table / sessions — nothing serialized `cancel`/`wg`/the session-publish-vs-snapshot across the two calls. The daemon shutdown path (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go` `runShutdownSequence`:904) calls `lldpMgr.Stop()` WITHOUT the `applySem` that `reconcileLLDP`->`Apply` (daemon_apply.go:2077) runs under, so a SIGTERM mid-commit races them: `wg.Add` vs `wg.Wait` (WaitGroup misuse — panic or dropped join), a data race on `m.cancel`, and a `Stop` that snapshots the session set before `Apply` publishes a later interface's session leaves that RX goroutine parked in `recv` forever (hangs shutdown / leaks the socket). Fix: a dedicated `lifecycleMu sync.Mutex` (distinct from `mu`) held by `Apply` across the whole teardown-then-rebuild and by `Stop` across teardown. Split the old `Stop` body into an internal `stopLocked()` (caller holds `lifecycleMu`); `Apply` calls `stopLocked()` (not `Stop`) to avoid re-acquiring the non-reentrant lock. `lifecycleMu` is never taken by the TX/RX/expiry goroutines (they take only `mu`), so holding it across `wg.Wait()` cannot deadlock. RED-on-revert VERIFIED under `-race`: reverting to the unguarded `Apply`(`m.Stop()`)/`Stop` made `TestApplyStopLifecycleRace` FAIL with WARNING: DATA RACE on `m.cancel` (Stop lldp.go:352) racing Apply's write + the WaitGroup/context internals, exit 1; restored -> `ok`. New test: pkg/lldp/lifecycle_mutex_5121_test.go (two goroutines hammer Apply/Stop 300x each, then assert coherent final teardown: not Running(), 0 sessions). Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; `go test -race ./pkg/lldp/...` ok; `go test -race -run LLDP ./pkg/daemon/` ok; gofmt clean. Docs: pkg/lldp/README.md gained an "Apply/Stop concurrency (#5121)" bullet + updated Apply/Stop entry-point lines. No cluster smoke (control-plane lifecycle race; no forwarding effect).
  **File(s)**: pkg/lldp/lldp.go, pkg/lldp/lifecycle_mutex_5121_test.go, pkg/lldp/README.md, _Log.md

The gRPC mocks define their own `Telemetry()` routing through the mock (the embedded `*dataplane.Manager` has a promoted `Telemetry()` that would otherwise wrap the raw Manager and bypass the injected error).   **Action**: #5052 [BUG cli LOW] The read-only rollback DISPLAY selectors truncated an out-of-range index through int32 and silently rendered the WRONG rollback slot with a success exit. `show system rollback [compare] N` (cmd/cli/show_system.go) and `show | compare rollback N` (cmd/cli/show.go handleConfigShow) parsed the selector with `strconv.Atoi` then cast `int32(n)`. On this 64-bit target `strconv.Atoi("4294967297")` succeeds, passes the `n >= 1` check, then `int32(4294967297) == 1` — so the ShowRollback/ShowCompare RPC carried slot 1 while the operator asked for a different (invalid) selector; the server (ShowRollback/ShowCompare in pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go) only validates the already-truncated positive value and cannot reconstruct the pre-truncation int. The mutating `rollback N` path already had the `ParseInt(_,10,32)` guard (#4868/#3447 in shared.go); these three display paths were missed. Fix (per the issue's fix direction — one shared parser): added `parseRollbackSelector(token, usage, min) (int32, error)` in cmd/cli/shared.go — `strconv.ParseInt(token, 10, 32)` returns `strconv.ErrRange` for any value outside int32 range instead of wrapping; `min` is 0 for the mutating `rollback` (0 = revert to active) and 1 for the read-only display/compare selectors that need a positive slot. Refactored the mutating rollback case to call it (min=0) and wired all three display paths through it (min=1). The `int32(n)` casts on the RPC fields were dropped (the helper already returns int32). ## 2026-07-10 — #5115 term-scoped next-hop-self

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: #5115 [BUG frr/bgp MEDIUM] `then next-hop self` widened into a
  neighbor-wide next-hop rewrite. `policy_render.go` scanned the effective
  export policy with `policyStatementHasNextHopSelf` and, if ANY term
  requested self, emitted `neighbor <peer> next-hop-self force` — an FRR knob
  that runs AFTER route selection and rewrites the next-hop of EVERY route
  advertised to the peer, including routes accepted by OTHER terms that never
  asked for self (semantic widening; can redirect traffic through the
  firewall or break third-party next-hop reachability). Fix: lower
  `then next-hop self` per-term INSIDE the export route-map as
  `set ip next-hop peer-address` + `set ipv6 next-hop peer-address`. In an
  OUTBOUND route-map `peer-address` resolves to the local session address
  (= self) and is evaluated per-route, so it rewrites ONLY the term's routes.
  Removed both neighbor-loop knob emissions (IPv4 + IPv6) and the now-unused
  `policyStatementHasNextHopSelf` helper. The outbound set-clause still
  overrides iBGP / route-reflector-reflected next-hops (keeps the #2977 fix),
  now correctly scoped; a bare `then next-hop self` term (no `from`) renders a
  match-all sequence and keeps neighbor-wide effect. Fail-on-revert tests
  (pkg/frr/frr_test.go): rewrote TestGenerateProtocols_BGPExportNextHopSelf
  and ...RRClient to assert the term-scoped set-clause + NO neighbor knob;
  added TestGenerateProtocols_BGPExportNextHopSelfTermScoped (the #5115
  two-accepted-term widening regression: prefix A accepted without self,
  prefix B accepted with self → exactly one set-clause, scoped to B's
  sequence, no knob); updated TestNextHopPeerAddress and
  ...BGPExportNoSpuriousNextHopSelf. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: restoring
  origin/master's policy_render.go (keeping the tests) made 4 tests FAIL
  (BGPExportNextHopSelf, ...RRClient, ...TermScoped, TestNextHopPeerAddress),
  no-spurious correctly stayed PASS; restored → all PASS. Validation:
  `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0;
  `go test ./pkg/frr/... ./pkg/config/...` ok; gofmt clean. Docs:
  pkg/frr/README.md `next-hop self` section + docs/phases.md rewritten to the
  term-scoped route-map contract. No cluster smoke (control-plane FRR config
  generation; verified by RED-on-revert unit tests).
- **File(s)**: pkg/frr/policy_render.go, pkg/frr/frr_test.go,
  pkg/frr/README.md, docs/phases.md, _Log.md
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix flowexport batch max-depth high-water update race (#5048).
  The `maxDepth` high-water update in `flowBatch.add()` ran OUTSIDE `b.mu`
  as a plain load-then-store (`if depth > maxDepth.Load() { Store(depth) }`),
  so two concurrent adders could interleave — B stores 2, A's later store
  of 1 clobbers it — regressing the published high-water mark. Replaced with
  a lock-free CAS-max loop (atomic `max(old, observed)`), consistent with the
  sibling `dropped`/`handoffDropped` atomics that also update outside mu.
  Added a test-only `maxDepthHook` seam and a deterministic barrier test that
  forces the reverse-order store (RED-on-revert: MaxDepth regresses 2->1) plus
  a 256-goroutine `-race` stress test. Docs: no contract change — maxDepth was
  already documented as a monotonic high-water mark; this only makes it correct
  under concurrency.
- **File(s)**: pkg/flowexport/transport.go,
  pkg/flowexport/maxdepth_race_5048_test.go

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: #5312 flowexport/ipfix — emit RECORD-granularity sampling IEs.
  ShouldExport does 1-in-N selection of whole SESSION records, but
  encodeIPFIXOptionsSamplerDataSet advertised PSAMP PACKET-selection IEs
  (selectorAlgorithm 304 / samplingPacketInterval 305 / samplingPacketSpace
  306, interval=1/space=N-1). A standards collector reads that as packet
  sampling and renormalizes each record's octet/packetDeltaCount by N —
  inflating the already-complete per-session volume. The only guard was a
  code comment ("must NOT multiply by N") that no wire field carried.
  Replaced with the RFC 7014 (Flow Selection Techniques) flow-selection IEs:
  flowSelectorAlgorithm (390, u16) = 1 (systematic count-based, IANA "Flow
  Selector Algorithm" registry), samplingFlowInterval (396, u64) = 1,
  samplingFlowSpacing (397, u64) = N-1. Record size 14 -> 22. A collector now
  scales the POPULATION (flow count/aggregate) by N and leaves per-record
  counters intact. Updated the sampler test to pin 390/396/397 + u64 widths +
  record size 22 AND assert 304/305/306 are ABSENT; proved RED-on-revert
  (reverting ipfix.go fails the template/data-set decode tests). Updated
  pkg/flowexport/README.md #3748/#5312 sampler section.

- **Action**: #5094 — ra join-timeout reclaimer no longer drops the owed
  replacement / terminal goodbye. Before the fix, when a draining sender's owner
  wedged past `claimWaitTimeout`, `releaseDrain` handed the tombstone to a

  losing the changed-config replacement (`onProvenClose`) and any owed

  precondition) so all #2033 invariants hold (≤1 live conn, ordered emit,
  claim-once, epoch/ifaceEpoch supersession, entry-identity guard). Made
  `onProvenClose` a bare `startLocked` closure and moved the #2834
  make-before-break `waitConnReady` into `releaseDrain` to avoid a data race
  on Apply-local state now that the closure runs in the reclaimer goroutine.

- **Action**: #5298 — install FRR reject/blackhole route for static-route
  reject/discard (fix the silently-erased `reject`). The schema
  (`schema_routing.go`) already accepted a `route <prefix> reject` leaf and

  (`buildRouteSnapshots`) so the fast path drops the prefix instead of
  LPM-matching a less-specific route; added `reject` display parity to CLI +
  gRPC `show route` and mirrored the `Discard` skip in daemon neighbor
  pre-resolution. Junos vs FRR semantics: Junos reject→FRR reject (ICMP),
  Junos discard→FRR Null0/blackhole (silent). Tests: end-to-end compile→FRR
  render (v4+v6, reject + discard) in pkg/frr, compiler-propagation (flat-set

- **Action**: #5120 routing/wireguard — unbind the WG TUN from its VRF on

  not-found device). Preserved `appliedRI` across the non-WG→WG same-name
  handoff so a reused anchor TUN's prior VRF claim carries into the WG

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: #5123 pkg/lldp — withdraw a neighbor immediately on a TTL=0
  shutdown LLDPDU. The RX path stored a TTL=0 frame like any other neighbor
  (ExpiresAt==now), so a departed peer stayed visible in `Neighbors()` until
  the next ~10s `expiryLoop` tick, violating IEEE 802.1AB shutdown semantics
  (the receiver must delete the neighbor at once). `rxLoop` now computes the
  `ifname/chassis/port` key and, when the parsed TTL is 0, calls the new
  `withdrawNeighbor` helper — a locked delete under the same `mu` the learn
  and expiry paths use — and does NOT cache the frame. A TTL=0 frame for an
  unknown key is a no-op (no error, no spurious insert). The non-zero TTL
  learn/refresh path is unchanged and the 10s reap cadence is untouched.
  Added three fail-on-revert tests driving the real `rxLoop` through the
  `recvFn` seam with a deterministic synchronous handshake: immediate
  withdrawal after TTL=0, unknown-key no-insert, non-zero learn+refresh.
  Proved RED-on-revert (the two TTL=0 tests fail on reverted source; the
  refresh test passes both ways by design). `go test -race ./pkg/lldp/...`
  green. Updated pkg/lldp/README.md neighbor-lifecycle + ParseTLVs notes.

  pkg/lldp/README.md, _Log.md
- **Action**: #5071 — preserve downstream giaddr + Option 82 on DHCP relay
  chaining (RFC 1542 §4.1.1 / RFC 3046). The forward loop stamped its own
  giaddr and Del/overwrote Option 82 unconditionally, even when the inbound
  BOOTREQUEST already carried a nonzero giaddr from a downstream relay —
  making the server pick the wrong pool, reply to the wrong relay, and
  destroying the original circuit-id. Added `giaddrIsSet()` and captured the
  chained condition BEFORE any mutation; on a chained request (giaddr!=0) the
  relay now preserves BOTH giaddr and the downstream relay-agent Option 82

    failures on a PRESENT DB. Clean abort (preflight is pure — no binary

## 2026-07-10 — #5455 tcp-flags operator-only fail-open fix
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5455 fail-open widening of a firewall filter. ParseTCPFlagsExpression now rejects a NON-EMPTY tcp-flags expression that sets no flag bits — operator-only ("&"), empty operand ("()"), and leading/trailing/duplicated "&" conjunctions ("& syn", "syn &", "syn && ack"). Added per-segment operand tracking (segHasFlag): a "&" with no flag operand on its left errors mid-loop; a final segment left empty errors after the loop; the historical `required==0 && forbidden==0 → (false,nil)` fall-through is now a fail-closed error. The legitimately-ABSENT case (expr=="" empty/whitespace) still returns (0,0,false,nil). Strict validator (validateFirewallTCPFlagsStrict) unchanged — it already rejects on err!=nil, so the new error makes "&"/"syn &" fail at commit instead of silently matching all TCP. Distinct from #4714 (dangling "!"). RED-on-revert proven: on origin/master "syn &" parses ok=true req=0x02 (drops trailing &); "&"/"()" return ok=false,nil (no constraint) and commit.

## 2026-07-10 — #5512 nft lo0 tcp-flags fail-closed fix
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5512 security fail-OPEN on the PRIMARY host-inbound path. The nft lo0 term lowering (nftRulesFromTerm, pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go) handled an UNREPRESENTABLE tcp-flags expression by DROPPING the constraint with a slog.Warn and emitting the term's configured verdict — widening an accept-term to admit ALL TCP. Now fails the term CLOSED: on ParseTCPFlagsExpression err, set tcpFlagsFailClosed and emit a per-TERM terminating `<match> meta l4proto 6 drop` overriding the term action (accept→denied, discard/reject→still deny, fall-through/PBR→terminate-drop). Mirrors the userspace direction (filters.go TCPFlagsUnparseable → Rust SnapshotIntegrityError::UnrepresentableFilterTCPFlags) but per-TERM so it never rejects the whole atomically-loaded lo0 table (that would leave NO host filter = fail-open). `meta l4proto 6` scopes the drop to TCP (a tcp-flags constraint only ever matches TCP in per_packet_l4_matches), so a tcp-flags-only term does not lower to a bare drop that denies ALL host-inbound traffic. Added tests: TestNftRuleFromTermTCPFlagsUnrepresentableFailsClosed (RED-on-revert proven: reverted arm emits `meta l4proto 6 accept`, the widen), TestLo0FilterPayloadUnrepresentableTCPFlagsParses (nft -c -f - parses the emission cleanly — no syntax error, no whole-ruleset failure). Full pkg/daemon suite green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go, pkg/daemon/lo0_filter_test.go, pkg/daemon/README.md, _Log.md

## 2026-07-10 — #5062 eventengine supersede producer-race fix
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5062 concurrency data-race / data-structure-integrity bug in the event-options action queue. HandleEvent evaluates under e.mu but RELEASES it before enqueue, so many RPM-probe goroutines run enqueue concurrently. On a full 64-slot queue enqueue falls into supersede(), which DRAINS accepted actions into a private slice (opening slots) then re-enqueues survivors; with no producer lock a second producer (enqueue fast-path send OR its own supersede) took a drain-freed slot between the drain and the re-enqueue, forcing supersede's refill `default` branch to DROP a survivor — an already-accepted action for a DIFFERENT policy — losing it + its FIFO position (miscounted queue_full). Fix: new e.enqueueMu serializes ALL producer-side queue mutation, held across the WHOLE enqueue (fast-path send AND supersede drain+refill), so the drain→re-enqueue is atomic w.r.t. other producers; the only concurrent actor left is the consumer (actionWorker, removes only), so a drain-freed slot is re-filled only by supersede itself → every survivor preserved exactly once in FIFO order. Lock ordering: enqueueMu is a producer-only leaf lock, NEVER held while e.mu is held (enqueue runs after evaluateEvent released e.mu) and the worker path (staleReason/armCooldown take e.mu) never takes enqueueMu → no cycle, no deadlock (channel ops under enqueueMu are non-blocking select+default). Added test-only afterDrainFn seam (nil in prod). Tests: TestSupersede_ConcurrentProducersConserveSurvivors (concurrent barrier: 64 producers × 40 rounds, conservation+FIFO) and TestSupersede_DrainStealWindowIsClosed (deterministic drain→steal→drop reproduction). RED-on-revert proven: removing enqueueMu drops a survivor (steal displaces seed63 deterministically; concurrent test loses+reorders seeds). Full pkg/eventengine -race suite green, new tests 10× flake-clean. Distinct from #2869 (same-policy ordering, not concurrent capacity theft).
- **File(s)**: pkg/eventengine/engine.go, pkg/eventengine/engine_supersede_race_5062_test.go, pkg/eventengine/README.md, _Log.md

## 2026-07-10 — #5047 fabric-listener supervision (retry + health)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5047 control-plane liveness gap: RunFabricListener (pkg/grpcapi/server.go) treated an lc.Listen failure as TERMINAL (return) and its Serve goroutine only slog.Warn'd while the owner blocked on ctx.Done — so a transient bind/device error OR a later Serve fault PERMANENTLY removed the network-exposed peer-proxy gRPC surface (monitor / peer-show / proxied-failover) until the whole cluster-comms lifecycle restarted; single-fabric deployments had no fallback. Rewrote it as a supervisor loop (superviseFabricListener) mirroring the project's monitorFabricState/runFabricStateSubscription pattern: bind → serve → on a fault (bind failure OR a Serve error that is NOT ctx-cancel/grpc.ErrServerStopped) retry after a BOUNDED exponential backoff (100ms base, 5s cap, reset to base after a Serve that stayed up >=30s) while ctx is live — keeps retrying a persistent bind failure at the cap without spinning, never gives up permanently. Expected graceful shutdown (ctx cancel → serveUntilDone returns nil; grpc.ErrServerStopped via errors.Is) exits cleanly, no retry. No goroutine outlives ctx (reuses serveUntilDone's buffered-errCh worker + bounded stopGRPCServer). Extracted buildFabricServer() (the #4107 auth + #4122 allowlist interceptor chains) and the fabricSupervisorConfig listen/serve seams for injection. Published per-bind up/down health via setFabricListenerUp / FabricListenerUp(addr) / FabricListenerHealth() for a status surface; transitions log at Info(up/stopped)/Warn(bind-fail/serve-fault), retry ticks at Debug (logging rules). Caller (daemon_ha_sync.go:582,585) unchanged — signature identical, supervision is internal. Tests (server_fabric_listener_5047_test.go, -race): (a) transient bind failures → REAL serve path (buildFabricServer+serveUntilDone over bufconn) recovers, health down→up; (b) ctx-cancel → supervisor + serve worker exit promptly, no leak, listen called once; (c) grpc.ErrServerStopped (wrapped) → clean exit, NOT retried; (d) persistent bind failure → bounded backoff, retry count under window/cap bound (no spin). RED-on-revert proven: patching the loop back to the pre-#5047 terminal return makes (a) [never comes up] and (d) [only 1 attempt] FAIL. Full pkg/grpcapi + pkg/daemon -race suites green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/grpcapi/server.go, pkg/grpcapi/server_fabric_listener_5047_test.go, pkg/grpcapi/README.md, _Log.md

## 2026-07-10 — #5032 SNMPv3 privacy salt uniqueness (monotonic counter)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5032 (codex-review-177 [A9-b1-F10], Low): SNMPv3 privacy
  parameters were INDEPENDENT random draws (`rand.Read(privParams)` per call in
  `encryptDES`/`encryptAES128`) with no per-key uniqueness state, so IV
  uniqueness was only birthday-bound — RFC 3826 §3.1.2.1/§3.3 (AES) and
  RFC 3414 §8.1.1.1 (DES) require the salt to be UNIQUE per (engineBoots,key).
  A DES-CBC IV = pre-IV XOR salt repeat leaks first-block structure; an
  AES-128-CFB IV = boots||time||salt repeat leaks plaintext XORs. Replaced the
  per-message random draw with a MONOTONIC 64-bit salt counter
  (`Agent.nextPrivSalt`, v3.go): seeded ONCE from crypto/rand (via the `randRead`
  seam) at first use — arbitrary boot-time start per RFC 3826 §3.3 — then
  incremented atomically (`privSalt atomic.Uint64`) for each encryption, so
  successive salts within an engine boot are guaranteed distinct, not merely
  probably distinct. `encryptPDU` allocates the salt and threads it into
  `encryptDES(privKey,data,salt)` / `encryptAES128(privKey,data,salt,boots,time)`
  (signatures changed to take the salt explicitly, return just ciphertext+err;
  caller echoes the salt as wire privParams). Preserved the RFC IV construction
  (preIV^salt for DES, boots||time||salt for AES) and the #5453 fail-closed
  guarantee — relocated to the seed: if the one-time seed draw fails,
  nextPrivSalt errors, encryptPDU propagates, buildV3Response drops the datagram
  (never a zero/predictable-salt PDU). Thread-safe: one-time seed under
  `privSaltMu`, each allocation a single atomic increment (concurrent response +
  trap encryption never collide). engineBoots (immutable per boot, monotonic
  across restarts) scopes the counter so a reboot re-randomizes the start.
  Tests: new v3_priv_salt_5032_test.go — TestPrivSaltMonotonicUnique (strict +1
  monotonic + uniqueness over 100k), TestEncryptPDUDistinctSaltsPerMessage
  (end-to-end via encryptPDU, +1 monotonic privParams over 2k),
  TestPrivSaltConcurrentUnique (16×5000 goroutines, all distinct, -race clean).
  Rewrote v3_rand_failclosed_test.go to assert fail-closed at the new seed layer
  (TestPrivSalt_RNGFailClosed, TestBuildV3Response_RNGFailClosed with a fresh
  never-seeded agent) + supplied-salt roundtrip/length-validation. Updated
  callers in agent_test.go, v3_seclevel_test.go, v3_priv_iv_test.go to the new
  signature (shared testPrivSalt helper). RED-on-revert PROVEN: patching
  nextPrivSalt back to an independent random draw makes both monotonic tests FAIL
  at i=1. `go build ./...` + `go test ./pkg/snmp/...` (and -race subset) green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/snmp/v3.go, pkg/snmp/agent.go, pkg/snmp/v3_priv_salt_5032_test.go,
  pkg/snmp/v3_rand_failclosed_test.go, pkg/snmp/agent_test.go,
  pkg/snmp/v3_seclevel_test.go, pkg/snmp/v3_priv_iv_test.go, pkg/snmp/README.md, _Log.md
## 2026-07-10 — #5064 EventBuffer drop-visibility (seq + overrun + metric)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5064 forensic-observability gap in the EventBuffer fan-out. `Add` fanned out non-blocking and took `default: // drop if subscriber is slow` on a full subscriber channel with NO counter, NO status, and NO sequence on the delivered record — a slow REST-SSE / gRPC event-stream / CLI-monitor consumer silently lost security/audit records and a forensic reader could not tell a gapped stream from a complete one. Fix adds three independent, in-band loss signals. (1) BufSeq: `Add` now stamps the buffer's monotonic publish sequence (`eb.seq`, from 1) onto every record BEFORE storing/fanning out — the SAME value stored in the ring, so a live subscriber and a `Latest()` snapshot agree; a BufSeq discontinuity between two delivered records pinpoints exactly which records were shed. Distinct from the reader-scoped `EventSeq` (#4915), which is 0 for the direct `Add` callers (health probes, HA replay). (2) Drop counters: per-subscriber `Subscription.dropped` (`atomic.Uint64`, accessor `Dropped()`) and aggregate `EventBuffer.droppedTotal` (accessor `DroppedTotal()`) increment on the drop path — no slog in the per-record path (CLAUDE.md logging rule). (3) Overrun flag: the fan-out arms a per-subscriber `overrun atomic.Bool` on a drop and stamps `EventRecord.Overrun=true` on the next successfully delivered record (per-subscriber copy so it is subscriber-scoped), giving a consumer that is not tracking BufSeq an explicit in-band "you lost records" signal; cleared once delivered. Exported the aggregate as Prometheus `xpf_event_stream_subscriber_dropped_total` (new `xpfCollector.eventStreamSubscriberDropped` desc, Describe+Collect emit guarded by `srv.eventBuf != nil`; declared-but-conditional emit is safe under the pedantic descriptor-coverage canary). Fan-out mutation is race-free (atomics; RLock unchanged). RED-on-revert PROVEN: restoring the old no-op `default` branch + dropping the BufSeq stamp fails `TestEventBufferDropVisibility` (sub.Dropped()=0, want 3). Gates: `go build ./...` green, `go test ./pkg/logging/... ./pkg/api/...` green, `-race` on the new tests green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/logging/eventbuf.go, pkg/logging/eventbuf_drop_visibility_5064_test.go, pkg/logging/README.md, pkg/api/metrics.go, pkg/api/metrics_descriptors.go, pkg/api/metrics_system.go, _Log.md
## 2026-07-10 — #5414 dhcp-relay untrusted client-forged giaddr / Option 82 anti-spoofing
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5414 (RFC 3046 §2.1). The #5071 chained-relay path trusted ANY nonzero inbound giaddr as a downstream-relay stamp and preserved it + its Option 82. Because the relay listens on a CLIENT-facing interface, a host on the client segment could forge a nonzero giaddr + crafted Option 82 to impersonate a downstream relay and steer the server's pool/policy selection (circuit-id/remote-id) or its reply. Fixed the trust point at pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go: gated the `chained` (preserve) decision on a new per-group trust flag — `chained := ir.trustOption82 && giaddrIsSet(...)`; `forgedGiaddr := !ir.trustOption82 && giaddrIsSet(...)`. On the DEFAULT untrusted interface a forged giaddr now falls through to the first-hop branch, which overwrites giaddr with the relay's own address (RFC 951/1542) and re-stamps Option 82 (addOption82 Dels the forged option first). The reset is counted in the new RelayStats.RequestsUntrustedGiaddrReset, incremented in the reset branch AFTER the hop-limit drop so a looping request is not miscounted. Added the Junos-parity config knob `overrides trust-option-82` (DHCPRelayGroup.TrustOption82) — compiled from all three parse shapes (flat-set/merged-Keys/block form), threaded through relaySpec.trustOption82 (participates in equal(), so a change restarts the relay) and interfaceRelay.trustOption82, and registered in setSchema for completion. ENFORCED, so no accepted-only advisory. Multi-hop relay preserved: on a trusted uplink (trust-option-82) the #5071 preserve behavior is intact. Tests: TestRunRelay_UntrustedForgedGiaddrOverwritten + _ResetCounted (pkg/dhcprelay) + TrustOption82 flat-set/default/merged+block/completion (pkg/config). RED-on-revert proven: reverting the trust-point to `chained := giaddrIsSet(...)` makes both new dhcprelay tests FAIL (giaddr + forged Option 82 preserved; counter 0) while the trusted #5071 preserve test still PASSES. Updated the #5071 chained test to drive the preserve path with a trusted config. `go build ./...` + `go test ./pkg/dhcprelay/... ./pkg/config/...` green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go, pkg/dhcprelay/relay_chain_5071_test.go, pkg/config/types_system.go, pkg/config/compiler_services.go, pkg/config/schema_routing.go, pkg/config/compiler_dhcp_relay_overrides_test.go, pkg/dhcprelay/README.md, _Log.md

## 2026-07-10 — #5281 grpcapi zeroize goes through the apply gate and stops xpfd
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: SECURITY. Fixed the gRPC `SystemAction{zeroize}` factory reset,
  which called package-level `performZeroizeWipe` directly with no lifecycle
  coordination and never stopped xpfd — so after a "successful" zeroize the
  still-running daemon held the pre-wipe in-memory ActiveConfig and the next
  reconcile / commit / HA-sync re-rendered the erased secrets (frr.conf /
  swanctl PSKs / Kea / login accounts) and re-created the `.configdb` SSOT.
  New daemon-owned `factoryReset` (pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go), wired as
  `grpcapi.Config.ZeroizeFn` (pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go), acquires the SAME
  `applySem` commit/apply/HA-sync serialize on (draining any in-flight apply),
  enters a TERMINAL reset generation (`d.resetting`) BEFORE the wipe, runs the
  wipe under the gate, and on success leaves the generation set (the handler
  stops xpfd moments later). Config writers now short-circuit on
  `errDaemonResetting`: commitAndApply / commitConfirmedAndApply / syncAndApply
  reject before persisting; executeConfirmedRollback skips; applyConfigLocked
  refuses (defense-in-depth); ipsecApplyForLeaseChange refuses (periodic swanctl
  PSK re-render). The grpcapi handler routes the wipe through `s.zeroizeFn`
  (falling back to a direct wipe only when nil), and on a fully-successful wipe
  schedules `scheduleStopDaemon` (`systemctl stop xpfd` after a 1s grace,
  mirroring the local `request system zeroize` CLI). Sequence is strictly
  gate → wipe → stop, fail-CLOSED: a wipe that does not complete returns
  Internal and does NOT stop the daemon. #4108 action-journal write preserved
  (before the wipe); existing RPC path unchanged otherwise. Sibling issues
  #5280 (wrong-root) / #5278 (per-principal auth) intentionally out of scope —
  no overlapping edits (this touches the gate/stop lifecycle, not the wipe roots
  or auth).
- **Tests**: pkg/grpcapi/zeroize_gate_stop_5281_test.go (gate→wipe→stop order,
  fail-closed no-stop, no-gate fallback — RED on revert to the direct-wipe
  handler: gate bypassed + no stop → FAIL, verified); updated
  system_action_journal_4108_test.go to neutralize the new scheduleStopDaemon
  seam; pkg/daemon/factory_reset_5281_test.go (gate-first acquire, terminal
  reset generation on success, gate released, commit/HA-sync/reconcile/ipsec
  rejected during reset, fail-closed clears the generation).
- **Validation**: `GOCACHE=/tmp/gocache-5281 GOTMPDIR=/tmp go build ./...` green;
  `go test -race ./pkg/grpcapi/... ./pkg/daemon/...` green; gofmt clean.

## 2026-07-10 — #4984 show interfaces: consistent authored/logical/kernel name identity
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #4984 (split from the #4884 interface-identity cohort, sub-defect B). The `show interfaces` family mixed name spellings for the SAME interface: summary + terse print the authored Junos name (`ge-0/0/2`), but the netlink-driven `detail` / `extensive` / `statistics` paths walked kernel netdevs and printed the Linux dash-form name (`ge-0-0-2`) as the interface identity. `detail` / `extensive` also keyed the zone + description joins by the authored name yet looked them up by the kernel name, so both were silently blank, and an authored-form filter (`show interfaces ge-0/0/2 detail`) reported "not found". Established one canonical model: the authored Junos name is the display identity across every variant; kernel names are used only for lookups. Added shared helpers in cli_show_interfaces_shared.go — `kernelToAuthoredMap` (config `LinuxIfName` reverse map: kernel netdev -> authored name), `authoredName` (resolve with kernel-name fallback for unmanaged devices), and `ifaceFilterMatches` (accept either spelling as the `<name>` filter). Routed detail/extensive/statistics display + zone/description joins + filter through the authored form (zone joins re-keyed by authored BASE name via `baseIfName`). Fixed the summary path's per-unit address lookup to resolve to the kernel VLAN sub-device (`config.LinuxIfName(physName)` + `.vlan-id`) instead of the authored `ge-0/0/2.50` — the authored form failed `net.InterfaceByName` and fell back to the parent, printing the parent's addresses under the sub-unit. Display-only change; no interface-management logic touched. `show interfaces queue` (CoS runtime snapshot, show_services_cos.go) is out of scope. RED-on-revert PROVEN: stashing the five source edits makes all four new tests FAIL (kernel identity printed / zone+desc joins blank / authored filter not found). Gates: `go build ./...` + `go test ./pkg/cli/...` green; gofmt clean.
- **File(s)**: pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces.go, pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_detail.go, pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_extensive.go, pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_stats.go, pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_shared.go, pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces_identity_4984_test.go, docs/junos-cli-reference.md, _Log.md

## 2026-07-10 — #5281 review fold: gate ip-monitoring route-overlay actuator
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: SECURITY (rev-5548 MERGE-NEEDS-MINOR fold). The initial #5281
  fix gated the daemon_apply.go writers + ipsecApplyForLeaseChange on
  isResetting(), but the ip-monitoring route-overlay actuator
  (actuateRouteOverlayLocked, pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go) was NOT gated. It
  acquires applySem and does a FULL re-render of /etc/frr/frr.conf
  (d.applyFRRConfig(d.assembleFRRConfig(...))) from the in-memory ActiveConfig.
  In the ~1s wipe->stop window (or graceful-shutdown drain), a probe flap with
  `services ip-monitoring` configured + a dirty overlay would acquire the
  just-released applySem, read the still-resident config, and RE-WRITE frr.conf
  — re-materializing the ERASED BGP-MD5/OSPF/IS-IS routing-auth keys into a
  world-readable file that SURVIVES the post-zeroize reboot, defeating the wipe.
  Added `if d.isResetting() { return false }` at the top of
  actuateRouteOverlayLocked (the frr.conf render chokepoint; returns false so
  the engine stays dirty — the daemon is being wiped/stopped so the retry never
  fires), matching the isResetting gates in daemon_apply.go.
  Audited the other ungated applySem acquirers: only ip-monitoring (frr.conf)
  and the DHCP-lease IPsec rebind (swanctl PSK, already gated via
  ipsecApplyForLeaseChange) re-render an erased secret. DNS writes
  /etc/resolv.conf (not wiped), proxy-ARP writes nft, the policy scheduler +
  NAT-pool alarm touch dataplane/in-memory state, and the host-tunables restore
  must run on shutdown — none re-render wiped state, so they stay ungated.
- **Tests**: pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon_test.go — TestActuateRouteOverlaySkipsWhenResetting
  asserts actuateRouteOverlayLocked is a no-op (returns false, RecordingExecutor
  ReloadCalls==0 so frr.conf is NOT re-rendered, no dp publish/bump) when
  isResetting() is true. RED-on-revert verified: removing the gate → the actuator
  renders frr.conf (ReloadCalls=1) + publishes → test FAILS.
- **Validation**: `GOCACHE=/tmp/gocache-5281 GOTMPDIR=/tmp go build ./...` green;
  `go test -race ./pkg/daemon/... ./pkg/grpcapi/...` green; gofmt clean.
- **File(s)**: pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go, pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon_test.go,
  pkg/daemon/README.md, _Log.md

  has dependent overlays. `fetch --install-libvirt` did

  (per-VM overlays are `qemu-img create -b <golden>`), so a re-fetch over an

  --output=json`) and `_dependent_overlays()` (scans sibling `*.qcow2` for
  backers of the golden); `_install_libvirt_golden()` now fails closed with a
  clear operator message (destroy dependents, or install under a fresh
  `--alias`) when the golden exists AND has dependents. First install and a
  re-fetch with no dependents still copy. Added 5 tests to
  test_xpf_deploy_disk.py (RED on revert: the overwrite-refused test loses its
  SystemExit when the guard is removed). Documented the golden-immutability
  contract in docs/distribution.md.
  Validation: `python3 -m py_compile scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` clean;
  `bash scripts/run-selftests.sh` green (38 passed, 0 failed); RED-on-revert
  proven (monkeypatched pre-fix copy -> overwrite-refused test FAILs).

## 2026-07-10 — ddns: tokenize multi-word ok-response (#5557 / claude-review-003 A10)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10 (fix/ddns-multiword-okresponse)
- **Action**: Fix a functional DDNS bug in the generic templated backend. A
  configured multi-WORD `ok-response` (e.g. `good nochg`) was stored as a
  SINGLE space-containing element `ok = []string{strings.ToLower(s)}`, but
  matchesGenericOK does WHOLE-TOKEN matching (#2838): a success token must
  equal a trimmed response line or be the leading whitespace-delimited field
  of a line. A space-joined element has a dead first-field path (a first field
  never contains a space) and can only match a line that is EXACTLY
  "good nochg", so a dyndns2-shape "good nochg <ip>" body — or a bare "nochg"
  line — was never recognized: every update treated as failed → error spam +
  backoff → DNS goes stale. Changed to `ok = strings.Fields(strings.ToLower(s))`
  so each configured word becomes a matchable whole token (the single-token
  shape of defaultGenericOKTokens). ANY-token (OR) matcher semantics unchanged.
  Added TestGenericMultiWordOKResponseTokenized (RED-on-revert verified: shape
  + end-to-end dyndns2/bare-word success cases fail on the old single-element
  code; single-word no-regression + default-set-untouched asserted). Updated
  pkg/ddns/README.md ok-response wording.
- **File(s)**: pkg/ddns/backend_generic.go, pkg/ddns/backend_http_test.go,
  pkg/ddns/README.md, _Log.md

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11 (fix/5578-policy-session-invalidation-errors)
  **Action**: #5578 propagate policy-session-invalidation failures instead of
  swallowing them to a log line. `clearSessionsForPolicyIDs` and its three
  wrappers (`clearSessionsForDeletedPolicies`,
  `clearSessionsForModifiedPolicies`, `clearSessionsForDefaultPolicyChange`)
  changed from `void` to returning an aggregated `error` (errors.Join of the
  ForEachV4/V6 enumerate errors + DeleteBatchKnownV4/V6 delete errors; both
  families always attempted first — a partial clear beats none). A partial
  invalidation is a stale-authorization gap: a failed enumerate leaves
  unvisited sessions and a failed batch-delete leaves matched sessions
  INSTALLED, so traffic the new policy should DENY keeps forwarding on old
  session state while the commit reported success. Added a combined helper
  `clearSessionsForPolicyChanges` that runs all three and joins. Callers now
  surface it: `applyAndSyncCommitted` joins it into the returned commit error
  alongside the non-fatal applyErr (mark-and-continue — config stays committed
  + still syncs to the peer, mirroring the surrounding apply-step discipline);
  `syncAndApply` returns it to `handleConfigSync`; the void confirm-timeout
  rollback (`executeConfirmedRollback`) logs it loudly (no return path — mirrors
  the applyConfigLocked slog.Error above it). slog.Error/Warn diagnostics kept.
  New fail-on-revert tests inject ForEach + batch-delete errors via the
  dataplane fake and assert the wrapper AND the caller RETURN the wrapped
  error (and, for the delete case, that the matched sessions remain installed
  = the observable stale-authorization gap). RED-on-revert proven: semantic
  swallow at the core (return nil) + caller ignoring the return → all three new
  tests FAIL. go build ./... + go test ./pkg/daemon/... green; gofmt clean.
  Updated docs/feature-gaps.md Policy-Rematch row with the #5578 error contract.
  **File(s)**: pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_invalidate.go, pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go,
  pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_invalidate_test.go, docs/feature-gaps.md, _Log.md

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11
  **Action**: #5572 review fold (rev-5590 MINOR) — fragment-associated deny is
  ALWAYS Deny, never reject. `fragDenyResult` now forces
  `r.Action = config.PolicyDeny` after building the matched result. A non-first
  fragment has no L4 header, so the dataplane cannot send a RST/ICMP — it can
  only silently DROP — and the Rust `frag_associated_deny_result` hardcodes
  `PolicyAction::Deny`. `isSkippedFragDeny` still accepts a skipped REJECT (a
  reject shadows the fragment identically to a deny), but the reported label is
  normalized to deny; a concrete L4 reject match still reports reject. Both
  verdicts are DROPs, so the #5572 false-permit is not re-introduced — this only
  corrects the deny-vs-reject label parity. Fixed the FragmentAssociatedDeny
  docstring + README fragment section (was "Action is deny/reject" — wrong).
  Added fail-on-revert reject-shadow test (RED-on-revert proven: removing the
  force reports Action=reject). Gates: go build ./... + go test -race
  policymatch/cmd-cli/grpcapi/api green; gofmt -w.

## #5449 dataplane/userspace bounds-check binding slot (inject + binding parse)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z
- **Action**: Fix unguarded binding-slot parse where `strconv.Atoi(args[2])` + `uint32(slotNum)` accepted "slot -1" and wrapped it to 4294967295 (later truncated by `uint16(req.Slot)` into a wrong source port / OOB binding-array slot). Added shared `parseBindingSlot` helper (control.go) that rejects negatives and values >= dataplane.BindingArrayMaxEntries ([0, MaxInterfaces*BindingQueuesPerIface)=1048576), comparing in int space so an over-uint32 value cannot alias a valid slot via truncation. Rewired both ParseInjectPacketCommand (inject.go) and ParseBindingCommand (control.go) through it, preserving each function's error-return shape. Added a defense-in-depth slot-range guard to validateInjectPacketRequestForHelper so a request built directly via BuildInjectPacketRequest with an OOB slot is also rejected at the helper seam. Bound sourced via existing `github.com/psaab/xpf/pkg/dataplane` import (userspace already imports dataplane; the reverse would be an import cycle) — no local mirror constant needed.
- **File(s)**: pkg/dataplane/userspace/control.go, pkg/dataplane/userspace/inject.go, pkg/dataplane/userspace/inject_slot_bounds_5449_test.go (new)
- **Validation**: go build ./... green; go test ./pkg/dataplane/... -count=1 all green; new SlotBounds tests pass; RED-on-revert proven (removing the parse guard makes "slot -1" return 4294967295 and the -1/at-bound/over-bound reject assertions fail; removing the validate guard lets Slot=4294967295 pass). Control-plane input validation only (CLI/gRPC inject-packet + binding parse) — no forwarding/dataplane-logic change, no cluster smoke required. gofmt clean.

## #5567 userspace-dp/icmp: consume generated-error token only after reply feasibility
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z
- **Action**: Fix cross-interface DoS where the shared per-reason GCRA rate-limit token (`allow_generated_error`) was consumed BEFORE the generated ICMP-error reply was proven buildable, so a flood of reply-eligible-but-UNBUILDABLE Time-Exceeded / Packet-Too-Big triggers on one interface (missing egress object, missing family primary address, fallible builder returning None) drained the global bucket and starved buildable PMTUD/traceroute diagnostics on another interface (false-deny). Chose build-first-then-token at BOTH sites (build == feasibility proof, gate the token as the final admission before emitting) — the only ordering that fully satisfies "builder returns None → no token spent"; mirrors the reject path's #3656 H11 build-before-consume ordering. SITE 1 `build_local_time_exceeded_request` (icmp.rs): moved the `allow_generated_error(TimeExceeded)` gate to AFTER the egress lookup + v4/v6 build. SITE 2 `compute_forwarded_egress_ptb` (tx/dispatch/mod.rs): build the PTB first, then `if built.is_some() && allow_generated_error(PacketTooBig)` — the `&&` short-circuit means an unbuildable PTB never touches the token; suppression gate still runs first; `mtu_signalled=true` (oversized-original drop) unchanged. Trigger-packet disposition (Some/None per input) identical to before; only WHEN the token advances changed.
- **File(s)**: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp.rs, userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/mod.rs, userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_icmp_te.rs (2 new #5567 tests + `global_bucket_test_lock` serialisation added to 5 existing bucket-dependent emission tests), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/tests/ptb.rs (2 new #5567 tests + lock added to 4 existing bucket-dependent tests), docs/generated-reply-rate-limit.md, _Log.md
- **Validation**: `cargo build` green; FULL `cargo test --release` green; new tests 5x flake-checked green. RED-on-revert proven: reverting BOTH sites to token-before-feasibility makes `te_unbuildable_missing_egress_does_not_drain_token_5567` (rate_limited_count 17≠1) and `ptb_unbuildable_missing_egress_does_not_drain_token_5567` (2≠1) FAIL. Fail-safe, non-forwarding, non-failover change (ICMP-error diagnostic generation path); loss-cluster iperf smoke deferred under the #1864 shim-ABI wall (verify-dataplane fail-closes cluster-deploy — a known lab blocker, not this PR). `cargo fmt` intentionally NOT run globally: the repo baseline is not rustfmt-1.9.0-clean (2062 files diff), so a global fmt would reformat the whole crate; additions match each file's existing hand-style.

## #5569 userspace-dp/reject: consume per-zone reject token only after output-filter classification
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z
- **Action**: Fix same-zone cross-protocol reject starvation where the per-zone reject GCRA token (`allow_generated_reject`) was consumed BEFORE the #2238/#3035 output-filter classification of the generated reply, so a flood of egress-FILTERED rejects (rejects whose generated ICMP/RST is discarded by the reply's OWN egress output filter / three-color policer) drained the ingress zone's shared reject bucket and suppressed a later TCP RST the SAME zone's output filter would have PERMITTED. Reordered `enqueue_reject_reply` (poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs) so `classify_generated_reply` + the `verdict.drop` check run BEFORE the `allow_generated_reject` token gate. New gate order: build (feasibility, #3656) → TX-frame budget → output-filter classify → per-zone token → enqueue. Same reorder pattern as #5567 (feasibility-before-consume for TE/PTB) applied to the reject bucket. Invariants: (1) a reply DROPPED by classify (verdict.drop incl. parse_error) spends NO token — the fix; (2) a reply that survives classify but the token denies is still dropped (rate-limited), `*_reject_rate_limit_drops` + aggregate `reject_rate_limited_total` bumped exactly once (allow_generated_reject called exactly once, no double-consume); (3) a survivor the token allows is enqueued with the SAME verdict.cos_queue_id/dscp_rewrite; (4) trigger disposition unchanged (caller drops on false return; build still happens first because classify reads the built &bytes). TX-frame budget gate kept in its prior relative order (queue-protection gate that refills, not an irreversible per-flood charge — not in scope; noted for a possible separate issue only).
- **File(s)**: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs (reorder classify-before-token + comments), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/reject_reply_tests.rs (3 new #5569 tests), docs/generated-reply-rate-limit.md, _Log.md
- **Validation**: `cargo build` green; FULL `cargo test --release` green (3916 tests across all binaries, 0 failures); the 3 new tests 5x flake-checked green. RED-on-revert proven: reverse-applying only the production reorder (tests kept) makes `egress_filtered_reject_does_not_drain_zone_token_5569` FAIL (a 1500-filtered-ICMP flood drains the per-zone bucket so the trailing filter-PERMITTED RST is denied; output-filter-drop count 1000≠1500). The two invariant-guard tests (token_exhausted_..._still_rate_limited, token_allowed_..._classify_verdict) hold in BOTH orderings by design (they assert rate-limiting + verdict threading are preserved, not the reorder). Fail-safe, non-forwarding, non-failover reject-diagnostic path; loss-cluster iperf smoke deferred under the #1864 shim-ABI wall. `cargo fmt` intentionally NOT run globally (repo baseline not rustfmt-clean); additions match each file's hand-style.

## #5171 userspace-dp/snapshot: run integrity build in defer_workers apply before ack/persist
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z
- **Action**: Close a fail-OPEN where the changed-plan `defer_workers=true` branch of `apply_snapshot` (`server/handlers/snapshot.rs`) ACKed `ok=true` and PERSISTED a snapshot as the boot baseline WITHOUT running the mandatory-map + forwarding integrity build that the non-defer reconcile path runs. A non-buildable config — bad interface address / CoS queue / NAT64 / NPTv6 rule, or a MISSING/UNOPENABLE mandatory BPF map pin — was acked + persisted, only to fail-open at the later deferred bring-up (whose re-apply/rebind failures are warning-only). Extracted the three PRE-TEARDOWN integrity legs that `Coordinator::reconcile` runs before it touches any live state into a side-effect-free `Coordinator::validate_snapshot_buildable(&self, Option<&ConfigSnapshot>) -> Result<(), ReconcileError>` (`afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/mod.rs`): (1) policy-state preflight via the new shared `snapshot::preflight_policy_state` (reconcile's inline #1606/#3402 preflight now calls the SAME helper — no drift, no duplication); (2) mandatory + present-optional map-pin openability via `snapshot::validate_map_pins` (opens each pin through the same `OwnedFd::open_bpf_map` then DROPS the fd — no retention, no `bindings` mutation); (3) full forwarding build via `snapshot::validate_forwarding_buildable` (the SAME `build_forwarding_state_with_policy_counters_and_previous` reconcile runs, but with SCRATCH policy+NAT counter stores so a rejected snapshot leaks no per-rule counter handles into the live stores, reading only the prior `self.forwarding`). `WgEngine::new` (invoked inside the build) is a pure constructor — no socket bind / thread spawn (those happen later in bring-up) — so a discarded scratch build has no observable side effect. The defer branch calls `validate_snapshot_buildable` BEFORE the side-effecting `prune_wg_control_threads_for_snapshot` / `prune_local_tunnel_sources_for_snapshot` and BEFORE the `guard.snapshot` swap, and fails CLOSED on error: restore the status generation/fib/at + capabilities bumped at the top of `apply`, `response.ok=false`, no `persist_state`, prior snapshot untouched — mirroring the #3766/#3789 same-plan capture-restore legs. Ordering choice: VALIDATE-BEFORE-PRUNE (the incoming snapshot is validated directly before the swap), so a rejected snapshot side-effects nothing — no prune runs, no snapshot swap, only the status bump is unwound. Defer semantics otherwise UNCHANGED: the worker spawn is still skipped (RETH MAC pending) — this adds integrity VALIDATION, not activation. Non-defer path UNCHANGED (reconcile_status_bindings already validates+builds).
  - Finding on the KEY QUESTION: `should_run_afxdp` is FALSE in the deferred apply (forwarding arming follows the deferred worker bring-up; the Go side also disarms before an unsupported publish). So `reconcile_status_bindings` cannot be reused in defer mode — when disarmed it takes the STOP path (`state.afxdp.stop()` + `Ok(())`: a teardown with NO integrity build), and when armed it would spawn workers (violating the defer contract). `validate_snapshot_buildable` is arm-independent by construction, which is why the integrity legs are run directly.
- **File(s)**: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/mod.rs (validate_snapshot_buildable + share preflight_policy_state in reconcile's inline preflight), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs (preflight_policy_state / validate_map_pins / validate_forwarding_buildable helpers), userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs (defer-branch validate + fail-closed restore), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/tests.rs (validate_snapshot_buildable_matches_reconcile_5171 parity test), userspace-dp/src/server/tests.rs (3 new #5171 defer handler tests), userspace-dp/src/main_tests.rs (#3789 test updated: gen-1 now buildable with a "lan" zone + ok map pins so it defer-accepts under #5171; missing-pin abort moved to gen-2), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/README.md, userspace-dp/src/server/README.md, _Log.md
- **Validation**: `cargo build` green; FULL `cargo test --release` green (0 failures); the 4 new tests 5x flake-checked green. RED-on-revert proven: neutralizing ONLY the defer-branch `validate_snapshot_buildable` call (tests kept) makes `apply_snapshot_defer_workers_missing_map_pin_fails_closed_5171` and `apply_snapshot_defer_workers_forwarding_integrity_fails_closed_5171` FAIL (the defer branch acks ok=true + persists the non-buildable config), while `..._valid_config_applies_without_spawning_5171` still passes. Fail-closed SECURITY fix on the non-forwarding config-application path; loss-cluster iperf smoke deferred under the #1864 shim-ABI wall. `cargo fmt` intentionally NOT run globally (repo baseline not rustfmt-clean); additions match each file's hand-style.

## #5171 review fold (rev-5605): validate_forwarding_buildable uses previous=None to avoid mutating live zone counters
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z
- **Action**: Fold a real side-effect leak found by the rev-5605 hostile review of PR #5605. Leg 3 `validate_forwarding_buildable` (`afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs`) called `build_forwarding_state_with_policy_counters_and_previous(snapshot, scratch_policy, scratch_nat, Some(&coord.forwarding))`. Inside the build (`forwarding_build/mod.rs` ~377-383) `state.zone_counter_store = previous.map(|p| p.zone_counter_store.clone())...; state.zone_counter_store.reconcile(&configured)`. `ZoneCounterStore` derives `Clone` over `Arc<Mutex<FxHashMap>>` (shares the inner map — `zone_counters.rs:143-146`) and `reconcile(&self)` is an in-place `.retain(|zid,_| configured.contains(zid))` UNDER THE SHARED LOCK — so passing `Some(&coord.forwarding)` for a VALIDATION build pruned the LIVE, published `coord.forwarding.zone_counter_store`, dropping cumulative per-zone traffic totals for any zone absent from the candidate snapshot. It fired even when validation later REJECTED (the zone-counter reconcile at build line 383 runs before the fallible filter_state/cos legs), mutating the live observability surface (`zone_traffic_counters()` → `show security zones` / REST / Prometheus) — contradicting the "side-effect-free" contract, and the fail-closed restore could not undo it. FIX: pass `previous = None` (drop the now-unused `coord` param; update the call site in `validate_snapshot_buildable`). Verified NONE of the fallible integrity legs (duplicate-zone-id, tunnel TTL, interface address, egress, route family/preference, neighbor family, NPTv6, filter unresolvable-token, CoS queue-id) reads `previous` for its accept/reject decision — every one faults on snapshot CONTENT only (`previous` feeds carry-over exclusively: NAT/source-NAT allocator reuse, cold-path slot retention, zone-counter totals, filter policer runtime), so accept/reject PARITY with reconcile is preserved while `None` gives the discarded build fresh default counter stores that touch no live state. `build_reconcile_forwarding` (the real apply build) keeps `Some(&coord.forwarding)` — carry-over is correct there.
- **File(s)**: userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs (previous=None + drop coord param + doc), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/mod.rs (call site + validate_snapshot_buildable doc), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/tests.rs (validate_snapshot_buildable_does_not_prune_live_zone_counters_5171 guard test), _Log.md
- **Validation**: `cargo build` green; FULL `cargo test --release` green (0 failures); new guard test 5x flake green. RED-on-revert proven: reverting `validate_forwarding_buildable` to `previous=Some(&coord.forwarding)` (re-adding the coord param) makes `validate_snapshot_buildable_does_not_prune_live_zone_counters_5171` FAIL (zone B pruned from the live store) while the 3 existing #5171 fail-closed defer tests + the parity test still PASS (verdict parity unaffected). Follow-up commit on the same branch fix/5171-defer-workers-integrity-build; not merged (team-lead re-verifies + merges).

## #5176 userspace-dp/nptv6: enforce static-NAT rule-set from_zone scope on translation
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z
- **Action**: Fix a security-domain crossing where NPTv6 (RFC 6296) translation ignored the static-NAT rule-set `from zone` scope. `nat_nptv6.go` already serialized `FromZone` on the `from_zone` snapshot field, but the Rust `Nptv6Rule` had no scope field and both lookup APIs (`translate_inbound`/`translate_outbound`) selected purely by prefix — so a rule scoped `from zone untrust` translated (and thus routed) NPTv6 traffic sourced from EVERY zone, and the #2241 overlap gate wrongly rejected legitimate per-zone split-horizon. Wire-mapping confirmed BOTH sides (Go `Nptv6RuleSnapshot.FromZone json:"from_zone,omitempty"`, Rust `#[serde(rename="from_zone", default)]`, same field position, serde_json transport): this consumes existing wire data — NO protocol bump. Added `Nptv6Rule.from_zone` + `zone_matches(zone)` (empty=wildcard, else exact). Threaded the packet's zone into both lookups and all 4 call sites: `translate_inbound` gates on INGRESS zone (poll_descriptor pre-routing `ingress_zone_name`; icmp_embed reverse path resolves ingress zone from `meta.ingress_ifindex`), `translate_outbound` on EGRESS zone (both poll_descriptor SNAT sites + the missing-neighbor seed site pass `to_zone`). Partitioned the #2241 overlap check by scope: two rules conflict only when their `from_zone`s can both match one packet (`zones_conflict` = either empty OR equal) — same-prefix/distinct-non-empty-zone pairs (split-horizon) are now admitted and resolve deterministically per zone.
- **File(s)**: userspace-dp/src/nptv6.rs (from_zone field + zone_matches + zone-gated lookups + zone-partitioned find_overlap/zones_conflict + module invariant doc), userspace-dp/src/nptv6_tests.rs (4 new #5176 tests + existing calls threaded), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs (3 call sites), userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/nat_match_v6.rs (embedded-reverse call site + ingress-zone resolve), docs/feature-coverage.md, _Log.md
- **Validation**: `cargo build` green; FULL `cargo test --release` green (0 failures). RED-on-revert proven: neutralizing `Nptv6Rule::zone_matches` to always-true makes `nptv6_zone_scope_gates_inbound_5176` + `nptv6_zone_scope_gates_outbound_5176` FAIL (wrong-zone packet gets translated); neutralizing `zones_conflict` to always-true makes `nptv6_split_horizon_same_prefix_distinct_zones_admitted_5176` FAIL (split-horizon rejected as overlap); `nptv6_wildcard_from_zone_matches_any_zone_5176` stays GREEN (no-regression). No Go change (FromZone already emitted). Security correctness fix on the NPTv6 translation path; loss-cluster iperf smoke deferred under the #1864 shim-ABI wall. `cargo fmt` intentionally NOT run globally (repo baseline not rustfmt-clean); additions match each file's hand-style.

## #5101 userspace/nat-static: invalid destination/mapped port fails CLOSED instead of collapsing to whole-address wildcard
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z
- **Action**: Fix a fail-OPEN NAT security bug where a static-NAT rule carrying a PRESENT-but-out-of-range `match destination-port` / `mapped-port` (e.g. a persisted / peer-synced 70000) collapsed to a whole-address 1:1 mapping that exposes EVERY port of the external address. `clampPort` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_static.go`) coerced any out-of-range port to `0`, but `0` is the VALID "port absent / match-any" wildcard sentinel — the Rust side (`static_nat.rs`, `(0, _) => (None, None)`) installs it as a whole-address entry. On the lenient load / peer-sync path (#1960) an invalid port therefore widened to whole-address — a fail-OPEN broadening, contradicting the code's "fails CLOSED" claim (the static-NAT analog of the §13 H12 SNAT/DNAT wildcard hole). Strict commit already rejects such a port (`validateNATMatchDestinationPortStrict` / `validateNATHostMaskStrict`), so reachability is mixed-generation / persisted-invalid (#5225/#5097 tolerant-path family). FIX (Go-only): added `staticNATPortOutOfRange(p) = p != 0 && (p < 1 || p > 65535)` — the same predicate the strict gate uses, preserving the absent(0)-vs-invalid distinction — and made `buildStaticNATSnapshots` DROP any rule whose `MatchDestinationPort` OR `MappedPort` is present-but-out-of-range, emitting an operator-visible `slog.Warn` (symmetric with the source-NAT unusable-pool + #3435 source-address lenient-path guards). An invalid port never reaches `clampPort` / the Rust `(0, _)` whole-address path — the rule fails CLOSED (no translation, no exposure). Genuine-absent (`0` → whole-address 1:1, a valid common shape) and valid in-range ports are unchanged. No Rust change, no wire change; `clampPort`'s misleading "fails CLOSED" comment corrected.
- **File(s)**: pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_static.go (staticNATPortOutOfRange predicate + drop-and-warn guard + clampPort doc fix), pkg/dataplane/userspace/static_nat_mapped_port_2491_test.go (replaced the buggy TestBuildStaticNATSnapshotClampsBadPort — which asserted the fail-OPEN clamp-to-0 as "fail closed" — with TestBuildStaticNATSnapshotOutOfRangePortFailsClosed + TestBuildStaticNATSnapshotAbsentPortWholeAddress no-regression twin), docs/userspace-dnat-plan.md (new §"Static-NAT invalid match destination-port fails closed (#5101)"), _Log.md
- **Validation**: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/`, `gofmt -l` clean; `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` green. RED-on-revert proven: neutralizing `staticNATPortOutOfRange` to always-false (reproducing the pre-fix clamp-to-0 behavior) makes `TestBuildStaticNATSnapshotOutOfRangePortFailsClosed` FAIL on all three subcases (match-out-of-range / mapped-out-of-range / both-out-of-range each produce a port-0 whole-address entry) while `TestBuildStaticNATSnapshotAbsentPortWholeAddress` (absent 0 → whole-address kept) and `TestBuildStaticNATSnapshotCarriesMappedPort` (valid 8080/80) stay GREEN. Go-only config-compilation fix on a non-forwarding path; no dataplane/cargo change, loss-cluster smoke not applicable.

  constant-time compare still runs unconditionally, preserving the #4157 timing
  profile.

## #5630 — IPsec typed endpoints bypass IP/FQDN validation (codex-181 M20)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11
- **Action**: Add strict-commit validation for every effective IPsec endpoint
  (IKE gateway address / dynamic hostname / local-address, and VPN

## 2026-07-11 — #5638: constrain master-password PRF to effective/supported scope (codex-review-181 M30)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11
- **Action**: Fixed masterPasswordPRF accepting an inactive/unapplied
  dormant or unsupported master-password PRF through the tolerant/HA
  persistence path → deterministic HA non-durability. Split it into two
  separable questions: (1) is encryption required? — fail-closed broad
  scan (masterPasswordConfigured), preserving #4705/#5231; (2) which PRF
  algorithm? — effective/applied scope only (effectiveMasterPasswordPRF:
  strip inactive + expand applied groups on a clone), accepting only a
  prfHash-supported selector, else the fixed supported default (sha256).
  A dormant/unsupported PRF can no longer reach prfHash and
  deterministically fail writeActive on HA config-sync.

  masterPasswordConfigured/effectiveMasterPasswordPRF/prfSupported helpers +
  defaultMasterPasswordPRF const), pkg/configstore/masterpw_dormant_prf_5638_test.go
  (new fail-on-revert tests), pkg/configstore/masterpw_apply_groups_5231_test.go
  (clarify unapplied-group comment for new effective-scope semantics),
  pkg/configstore/README.md (crypto hardening note).
- **Validation**: `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./pkg/configstore/...
  ./pkg/config/...` green; gofmt clean. RED-on-revert proven: reverting
  masterPasswordPRF to the pre-fix over-broad superset makes all four new
  tests FAIL — masterPasswordPRF returns "bogus"/"sha512", WriteActive fails
  with "unsupported master-password pseudorandom-function \"bogus\"", and

## 2026-07-11 — #5645 feeds first-fetch deny fail-open (codex-review-181)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11
- **Action**: Fix fail-open where a direct feed-bound DENY name published as an
  empty (match-none) overlay entry BEFORE the first successful fetch — the deny
  compiled to match-none so denied traffic was PERMITTED for the whole
  pre-first-fetch window. SnapshotForBindings now OMITS a binding whose feeds
  all lack an installed snapshot (len(merged)==0), leaving the name UNRESOLVED
  so the policy lowering fails CLOSED (unrepresentable -> __unsupported_address__
  -> whole-snapshot preflight reject, the #3261 contract). Integrates with the
  #5282 re-fetch window: a persisted feed carries its last-good snapshot forward
  and still resolves to prefixes, so it stays published.

  pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_addrbook.go (buildAddressBookTableWithFeeds
  doc corrected), pkg/dataplane/userspace/feed_enforcement_test.go
  (TestEmptyFeedSnapshotYieldsNoPrefixes docstring corrected),
  pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_observability.go (unknown-feed posture
  comment corrected for #5645), pkg/feeds/README.md (#5645 first-fetch
  fail-closed section + cold-start line).
- **Validation**: `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./pkg/feeds/...
  ./pkg/config/... ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/... ./pkg/daemon/...` green; gofmt

## 2026-07-11 — #5646 feeds publication-debt (rejected apply suppresses retry)

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-11
- **Action**: Fix installSnapshot committing content hash before the void
  onUpdate callback → a REJECTED apply suppressed retry of identical content
  (publication debt / fail-open). Design (a): split published-hash from
  installed-content hash; onUpdate void→error; publishedHash advances only on a
  confirmed (nil) apply, so an identical refetch after a rejected apply re-fires
  and retries on the normal refresh cadence (no thrash on success).

  pkg/feeds/feeds_publication_debt_5646_test.go (fail-on-revert, RED proven),

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-12
- **Action**: #5709 fix (codex-review-182 M36) — prevent a DDNS wire-RR
  cross-scope clobber. Two DDNS scopes (e.g. two redundancy groups, or a
  per-interface + global binding) can resolve the same host to the same
  address and CO-OWN one wire resource record; each keeps a distinct
  ownership row (ScopeKey prefix) but on the wire there is ONE RR. Because
  `deleteOwnedLocked` reconstructed the wire RR from {FQDN, ForwardType,
  Address} alone, one scope's teardown (lease expiry / config removal)
  issued a wire DELETE that removed the RR the OTHER scope still owned —
  clobbering a live record. Added `wireRRSharedWithOther(owned)`: when
  another store row (a different scope) carries the same canonical FQDN +
  forward type + rdata, `deleteOwnedLocked` SUPPRESSES the wire delete,
  releases only the departing scope's claim, and leaves the live RR for the
  surviving scope (reference-count decrement over the claim table; equal
  {FQDN, Address} implies an equal reverse PTR so both directions are
  covered). Runs before the wire op and is backend-independent. Counted via
  `Stats.DeleteCoowned` + `xpf_dhcp_ddns_skipped_total{reason="coowned"}`.
  Added fail-on-revert test `TestCoOwnedWireRRSurvivesOtherScopeTeardown`
  (RED proven by neutralizing the guard: RG1 teardown deleted the co-owned
  RR; GREEN restored). gofmt clean; pkg/ddns + pkg/api suites green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/ddns/manager.go, pkg/ddns/scope_test.go,
  pkg/api/metrics_system.go, pkg/api/metrics_descriptors.go,
  pkg/ddns/README.md

  policy section from m.lastSnapshot, then stamped next.Config = cfg +

  ordinary ApplyConfig failure leaves lastSnapshot at the OLD policy while

  actuator then pass the NEW cfg). Added a fail-closed guard
  (routeOnlyPublishHybrid): refuse the publish when cfg is not the config
  lastSnapshot was compiled from (pointer fast-path + reflect.DeepEqual
  fallback so a distinct-but-equal config is never falsely refused). On refusal
  the OLD consistent snapshot stays live and the desired-overlay cache stays at
  baseline (#3760). Added fail-on-revert test (RED proven with the guard
  neutralized: publish returns nil error + appliedSnapshot advances to cfgB +
  hybrid shipped to helper) plus a false-refusal guard test. Composes with
  #5679 (commit already fails via applyErr; this stops the manager's applied
  identity from lying). gofmt clean; pkg/dataplane/userspace + pkg/daemon green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_overlay.go,
